items.title: Ira Gitler interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: When he and his brother Branford came with Art Blakey and people heard them

ctx.x: Well I think it has surfaced in jazz because I’ve written about this also and no one has really picked up on it. I thought that the continuity of jazz in the black community was kind of co-opted by radio and television. I don’t say that rhythm & blues wasn’t great, I used to enjoy it very much, and other forms of black music, of course Gospel, if you’re not moved by that I think you’re ready for the grave. You know there’s all forms. But there are certain commercialized musics in, you know, coming from all areas…

communities when I was in college and in my post-college years, and connect with people because we all had the same records and we were listening to the music together and all that. And then I found more and more that the young black people coming up didn’t know anything about jazz because they didn’t hear it anymore. And the advent of Wynton Marsalis has brought, as you know, a raft of great young black musicians. They weren’t coming to the music, not only was the black community not listening to it, but as a…

Can — and this is kind of a follow-up — can jazz, you know for instance we talk about the big band period and we say how two great things, people were dancing and people were listening on the radio. Can jazz ever become America’s popular music again?
